classification.difficultyReason: A short modelling set. Total revenue and cost are built from per-person or per-ticket quantities, then subtracted and expanded. It needs interpretation of the profit structure but has no geometry or elimination of a variable.

content.prompt: Show that the profit $P$ in dollars in each situation is given by the stated equation.

children.label: a
children.prompt: A tour operator's expense per person for a group of $x$ people is $E=300+200x$ dollars. Each person pays $C=1100-100x$ dollars. Show that the profit is $P=800x-300x^2$.

answer.worked:
Profit per person = Cost − Expenses
$$\begin{align*}C-E&=(1100-100x)-(300+200x)\\C-E&=800-300x\end{align*}$$
Total profit = Number of people × Profit per person
$$\begin{align*}P&=x(800-300x)\\P&=800x-300x^2\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: A Melbourne theatre company sells $x$ tickets at a price of $p=90-3x$ dollars each. Its costs are a fixed $\$500$ plus $\$15$ per ticket. Show that the profit is $P=75x-3x^2-500$.

answer.worked:
Revenue = Number of tickets × Price
$$R=x(90-3x)=90x-3x^2$$
Costs:
$$C=500+15x$$
Profit = Revenue − Costs
$$\begin{align*}P&=90x-3x^2-(500+15x)\\P&=75x-3x^2-500\end{align*}$$
